yussef.title: Black Focus — album notes
yussef.summary: Describes London musical influences and the duo’s early performances in Peckham and Camberwell.

moor.title: Black Encyclopedia Of The Air — release announcement
moor.summary: Identifies Moor Mother as Philadelphia-based in September 2021.

nancy.title: Ghetto Reality — catalogue and album notes
nancy.summary: Documents the project with Nancy Dupree’s elementary-school pupils in Rochester, New York.

steve.title: Only You — reissue notes and artist interview
steve.summary: Connects the original album to the Nigerian boogie scene and producer Nkono Teles.

nkono.title: Love Vibration — retrospective notes
nkono.summary: Documents the producer’s work in Lagos and his collaborations with Nigerian musicians.

sexual.title: I Need A Freak — expanded reissue notes
sexual.summary: Documents the original album’s recording in Akron; the reissue adds later singles.

jimetta.title: How Good It Is — album notes
jimetta.publisher: Jimetta Rose & The Voices of Creation / Day Dreamer
jimetta.summary: Describes Jimetta Rose’s Los Angeles scene and community choir.

contact.title: Dancing Inner Space, 1982–1984 — liner notes
contact.summary: Links the project to Andy Sojka, Rick de Jongh and their Holloway Road label operation.

okvsho.title: Traphouse Jazz — album notes and credits
okvsho.summary: Explicitly locates the Boyoom Traphouse recording studio in Zurich.

alma.title: Visions — artist biography
alma.summary: The band’s own biography states that it formed in Basel.

flofilz.title: Speakthru — artist biography
flofilz.summary: The artist describes his work as jazz-sample-based beatmaking from Germany.

debich.title: Zbliżenie — archive notes and session credits
debich.summary: Lists Radio Łódź sessions from 1974 to 1977, with musicians and individual recording dates.

compro.title: Simurg — collaboration notes
compro.summary: Describes the Ghent collective’s collaboration with Istanbul musician Murat Ertel and singer Esma Ertel.

nightforce.title: Dance — reissue notes
nightforce.summary: Distinguishes the European title track from its slower South African edition and added Tom Cats tracks.

lafayette-label.title: Soul Makossa — historical reissue notes
lafayette-label.summary: Documents the group’s move to Paris, collaboration with Manu Dibango and Hihache’s later sampling history.

vaughan.title: Feel My Love — reissue notes
vaughan.summary: Provides the 1983 album context and describes its later Orange County boogie association; this is not a recording location.

azmari.title: Samā’ī — album notes
azmari.summary: Documents Brussels formation in 2015, Istanbul performances, and study of Turkish and Ethiopian scales.

free.title: Free Music (Part 1) — archival reissue notes
free.summary: Identifies Najib Alhoush and The Free Music with Libya; describes a retrospective compiled from several albums.

habibi.title: Habibi Funk 007 — curatorial notes
habibi.summary: Describes a personal selection across multiple musical cultures, explicitly rejecting a single historical genre.

habibi2.title: Habibi Funk 015 — curatorial notes
habibi2.summary: Names Egyptian, Moroccan, Libyan, Lebanese and Algerian material, plus a musical connection between Kenya and Oman.

archie.title: The Archie Pelago EP — label notes
archie.summary: Introduces Archie Pelago as a live band from Brooklyn.

malik.title: In A Better Way — release notes
malik.summary: Identifies Malik Alston and collaborators Jason Hogans and John Arnold with Detroit.

lockhart.title: The Aquarius Years — artist page and credits
lockhart.summary: Documents the featured musicians and earlier release history; the artist’s own profile currently identifies Los Angeles.

edlongo.title: The Other Fantasy — recording notes
edlongo.summary: Describes multiple recording sessions around Europe without naming the cities.

mauskovic.title: Down In The Basement EP — album notes
mauskovic.publisher: Soundway Records / The Mauskovic Dance Band
mauskovic.summary: Explicitly links the Amsterdam group’s music to Afro-Colombian styles and picó culture.

pino.title: Pino Daniele — official biography
pino.summary: Documents Neapolitan musical roots and the combination of local song with blues, jazz and rock.

nile.title: Nile Rodgers — inductee biography
nile.summary: Documents the guitarist’s professional work in the Apollo Theater house band in Harlem.

sahib.title: Companionship — liner notes and recording credits
sahib.summary: Lists several Cologne sessions and another venue; no assumption that the unidentified EP uses identical takes.

gino.title: Gino Soccio — artist catalogue
gino.summary: The catalogue identifies Montréal, Québec as the artist’s origin, rather than merely a birthplace.

george.title: George McCrae — biography by Bill Dahl
george.summary: Describes McCrae as a Miami-based performer associated with the early disco scene.

westlake.title: Studio A — studio history and address
westlake.summary: Documents the studio’s connection to Thriller and identifies its Los Angeles address.

dabeull.title: Intimate Fonk — artist biography
dabeull.summary: The release biography describes Dabeull as Parisian and discusses his funk production practice.

esther.title: Esther Williams — founder biography
esther.summary: Documents the singer’s professional career and musical community in Washington, DC, including her Friends & Company recordings.

soulsearchers.title: The Soul Searchers — artist history
soulsearchers.summary: Documents the Washington, DC band and the extensive sampling history of Ashley’s Roachclip.

maynard.title: Maynard Ferguson — biographical exhibit
maynard.summary: Documents the bandleader’s relocation to New York in 1973 and the subsequent recording period.

mos-museum.title: yasiin bey: Negus — press release, October 17, 2019
mos-museum.summary: Identifies yasiin bey as Mos Def and explicitly describes Brooklyn as his hometown. Direct PDF retrieval timed out; the relevant publisher text was read via its indexed primary-source result.

swedien.title: Bruce Swedien on Thriller, track by track — Beat It section
swedien.summary: Engineer Bruce Swedien recalls Eddie Van Halen recording the Beat It guitar solo at Westlake Studio B.
